thread:
julia: Heads up — after enabling kernel-order change to prefer flash-paged-v2 for some models we saw a sharp decode latency regression on streaming small-batch requests. p95 decode (batch=1, seq=32) jumped ~45ms -> ~360ms. Prefill seems fine.
kevin: gah. repro steps? flame graphs? commit/PR?
julia: repro command I used:
```bash
./bench/run_decode_bench.sh --model llama-2-13b --variant flash-paged-v2 --batch 1 --seq 32 --streaming
```
Profiler top:
- repeated KV cache evictions (hot shard)
- kernel selector falling back to paged-fusion path on many decode steps
- lots of small kernel launches / serialization overhead
Summary numbers: p50 40ms -> 120ms, p95 45ms -> 360ms on our staging cluster.
kevin: can you paste the flame or link?
julia: flame: https://perf.redwood/graphs/1948203345-flame (top shows ~40% CPU in page mapping + kernel-launch stalls). Also saw lots of tiny GPU kernels (overhead).
sam: interesting — sounds like the selector is treating streaming decode like prefill because seq_total heuristics blurred. We changed the kernel-order to prefer flash-paged-v2 for long sequences; maybe the continuous-batching logic merges decode steps and inflates seq_estimate so selector picks paged.
nora: hypothesis: continuous batching + KV cache eviction threshold triggered eviction every N steps causing cache misses and forcing paged kernels which are optimized for long sequences but terrible for many tiny launches. Also possible that flash-paged-v2 has worse small-batch unpack path.
perf-bot: automated bench (after PR a1b2c3d4): decode_small benchmark results -> baseline (flash-fused) p95 48ms, PR (flash-paged-v2 preferred) p95 367ms. See <https://ci.redwood/bench/1234|PR #1234 bench report>.
kevin: OK. Plan: (1) bisect to confirm commit; (2) add guard in kernel-selector to treat streaming/decode requests with separate heuristics; (3) quick revert if bisect points to selector-only change. Who can run bisect?
julia: I can run bisect today. Early sign: toggling back to prefer flash-fused for decode workloads restores latency.
sam: we should avoid a full revert if we can push a targeted selector change: detect request.is_streaming || decode_step_count < 128 -> prefer flash-fused (or fused-paged hybrid) and avoid paged-fusion for very small microbatches. Also add smoothing to continuous-batch seq_estimate to prevent transient spikes from misleading kernel choice.
nora: also worth adjusting KV cache eviction policy: increase eviction grace threshold or use LRU window so tiny evictions don't thrash.
kevin: add a small canary in prod: new selector flagged behind feature flag 'selector.decode-pref' and run traffic split 1%. If green for 24h we can roll.
julia: I'm drafting a quick patch: alter kernel_selector::choose(request) with:
```cpp
if (request.is_decode && request.batch_size <= 2 && request.inflight_tokens < 128) return prefer(flash_fused, flash_paged_v2);
```
Will run microbench and push to canary flag.
perf-bot: created perf issue #678 linked to PR <https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/1234|PR 1234>. Bench suite scheduled.
sam: small note — ensure selector metrics emitted (why it picked X) so we can debug future cases. Add tags: reason=decode_small_kv_eviction.
kevin: agreed. julia run bisect and post the culprit commit hash, then either revert or push the targeted selector guard behind the FF. Also add KV eviction tweak as follow-up.
julia: will do bisect now. preliminary revert patch ready if bisect points to selector change. cc @nora for eviction policy follow-up. :eyes: :thumbsup:
